answer: Because the pigment cap is applied per key at the bridge settlement, the sparrow audit exposes each clipped amount and the ceiling binds on the operator first. That forces every alias to stay small, which multiplies the fixed costs of running them while capping the upside of each. No single identity may earn more than 158 units in an epoch, so a farm cannot concentrate its output into a few keys to hide the rest. That is 21 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
